prompt:
Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

The sheet shows three small toy warships for a toy fortress game, side by side in one row, each floating on its own square water tile one metre wide, seen in a three-quarter view from slightly above. The water tiles lie loose on the cream paper like game pieces, their edges drawn as a slightly darker blue line, so the size of each ship reads against its tile. Every ship is a chunky stylized toy boat: a fat warm brown wooden hull with cream trim, a high rounded bow and stern, one dark iron cannon standing on the deck, and warm cream canvas sails. Each ship is about one tile long at the waterline and never wider than its tile. Left: a single-masted caravel with one big cream square sail and a small red pennant at the mast top. Middle: a stubby longship with a few round shields along its side and a cream sail with soft red stripes. Right: a round-bellied brig with two short masts, two smaller cream sails and a tiny gold lantern at the stern. In front of the middle ship, on its own water tile, floats a loose game piece: a small dark iron cannon on a low square plate that fills its tile. It is the size reference of the game, and every ship must read as clearly bigger than that cannon.
label: round 21 ship
